subject: nutrition-food-science
title: Protein Denaturation: Egg White Sets Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: A student says the white sets because its water leaves as it cooks. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - setting means the water has left
The water stays trapped in the protein network - heat unfolds the chains and they bond and set.
The yolk pushes the water out of the white as it cooks
The pan absorbs the water out of the white

questions.misconception: The white sets because the heat dries the water out of it.
questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: The white sets because the heat dries the water out of it. Reteach point: The water stays trapped in the protein network - heat unfolds the chains and they bond and set. Gentle heat unfolds the folded protein chains in the egg white, the unfolded chains bond to each other and form a network that traps the water inside it, and the white turns opaque and sets firm with its water still held in the network.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain what gentle heat does to the protein chains.
questions.answer: Gentle heat gives the folded protein chains energy to open out, unfolding each tight coil into a long loose chain.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names unfolding, not drying: the chains must open out before they can bond into a network.

questions.prompt: At the bonding stage, what has happened inside the white?

choices.text: The white has already been lifted out of the pan, fully set
The unfolded chains have linked with new bonds into a network that traps the water
The chains have folded back into tight coils
The water has left and the white is dry

questions.feedback: Scene 3 shows bonding: the unfolded chains net together and the white turns opaque as the water is trapped in the network.

questions.prompt: State the final stage of the change and say why the set white holds its shape.
questions.answer: The white is fully set, opaque and firm, because the bonded protein network holds its shape with the water still trapped inside it.
questions.feedback: Credit the network reasoning: the white holds its shape because the bonded chains form a network, not because anything left it.
